縫.meaning: A soldier in a <part>lookout post</part> on a hill rips his trousers. Bored, he lowers a <part>thread</part> down the long <part>ramp</part> to his grandmother at the bottom, who ties a needle to it. He hauls it up and spends the whole night watch learning to <kanji>sew</kanji>.
縫.on: Next she sends up a garden <sound>ho</sound>se, so he can water the flowers on the roof.
縫.kun: He sits in a quiet <sound>noo</sound>k of the tower, stitching.

窮.meaning: A hunter is so broke he lives in a <part>hole</part> in the hillside. His <part>pot belly</part> has shrunk flat, and he has sold everything but his old <part>bow</part>, which he plays like a fiddle for coins. A rabbit drops him a carrot out of pity. He's truly <kanji>hard up</kanji>.
窮.on: He even swaps his last arrow for a broken pool <sound>cue</sound>.
窮.kun: Then he digs up a rusty <sound>key</sound> and cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!': it opens a treasure chest at last, the very end of his bad luck.

妥.meaning: A <part>woman</part> runs the claw machine at the fair, and children keep crying when the metal <part>claw</part> drops their prizes. So she oils it, tunes it and slows it right down, until it lowers each teddy into a child's arms as softly as a kiss. Now it's the most <kanji>gentle</kanji> machine at the fair.
妥.on: Its favourite prize is a yellow rubber <sound>du</sound>ck, which it sets down on the counter without a squeak.

盆.meaning: A potter drops her best flat <part>dish</part> and it breaks into a dozen pieces. She glues each <part>part</part> back with its edge tilted up, so it comes out deeper than before. Rain fills it overnight, and by morning two sparrows are splashing in her new <kanji>basin</kanji>.
盆.on: She dries the shivering sparrows beside a crackling <sound>bon</sound>fire in the yard.

騰.meaning: A <part>horse</part> discovers the children's trampoline in the garden. Boing: over the fence. Boing: over the shed. Her owner, a <part>flailing man</part> in slippers, runs round underneath with a bucket of oats, begging her to come down. By lunch she's sailing past the pale daytime <part>moon</part>, still <kanji>leaping up</kanji>.
騰.on: When she finally lands, she stamps on his big <sound>toe</sound>, and he hops round the garden.
騰.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' yells the owner, waving a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic to tempt her back down.

胞.meaning: Before a baby is born, it gets a packed lunch every day: a soft round cushion, pale as the <part>moon</part>, where the mother can <part>pack up</part> food and air and send them down a cord. Nine months of deliveries. When the baby arrives, the empty lunchbox follows: the <kanji>placenta</kanji>.
胞.on: The new dad is so excited he waters the whole street with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.

卑.meaning: The palace's newest servant gets the lowest job of all: weeding the king's <part>rice field</part> <part>ten</part> times a day, bent double, while a <part>slash</part> of muddy rain runs down his back. Even the king's goat outranks him. No job in the land is more <kanji>lowly</kanji>.
卑.on: The goat even nibbles the <sound>hee</sound>l of his boot while he works.
卑.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' he squeals, as the goat runs off with his ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn.
